issue: Does the oath requirement in 18 U.S.C. § 1546(a)'s paragraph four (false statements 'under oath') also apply to the separate 'knowingly presents' offense in that paragraph?

sides.position: The 'knowingly presents' clause stands alone and does not require that the false statement have been made under oath.
cases: United States v. Khalje, 658 F.2d 90 (2d Cir. 1981)

sides.position: The oath requirement applies to the 'knowingly presents' clause, so presenting a false document not sworn under oath is not a violation.

quote: Other circuits are split on this question.
cite: United States v. Oluwatoyin Aborisade, No. 24-4466 (4th Cir. 2026)
